name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,204

solutions.check: 28 entries, 58 crossings, 0 conflicts, agrees with the 27 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Rodent died after turning tail, last to go

indicators.note: having turned round, the abbreviation is read from the end
the last going away means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: ob., short for Latin obiit, means died, as on gravestones
the tail of something is its back or rear end

explanation.surface: A rodent died after turning tail and fleeing, the last of its kind to go.
explanation.walkthrough: OB reversed + BAC(K). 'Turning tail' reads as running away, but 'turning' goes with 'died' and 'tail' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobac is the steppe marmot of eastern Europe and Asia, a burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Pub poured writer a port

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
a liquid that poured ran
a quill pen is a writer
taken as written

explanation.surface: At the pub, a writer had a glass of port poured for him.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR + RAN + QUILL + A. 'Port' looks like the fortified wine that goes with the pub, but it is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Barranquilla is Colombia's chief Caribbean seaport, at the mouth of the Magdalena River.

clue.text: Pack up — and take part of the dessert

indicators.note: taking a part of a word means using only a piece of it, here its final letter

blocks.note: to pack up and to bomb both mean to fail or break down
the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A diner is told to pack up and take some of the pudding home.
explanation.walkthrough: BOMB + E. The E is just a fragment of 'the', which reads as part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a frozen dessert moulded into a dome, often ice cream in layers.

clue.text: Like some finely made books that would get a younger one over the moon?

definitions.text: that would get a younger one over the moon?

blocks.note: first meaning: having covers of calfskin leather

blocks.clueFragment: that would get a younger one over the moon?
blocks.note: second, cryptic meaning: in the nursery rhyme the cow jumped over the moon, so her calf would need to be bound for it

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle has the cow jump over the moon; her calf, the younger one, would leap or bound there too.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf-bound book has covers of calfskin leather, a mark of fine bookbinding.

clue.text: Arrest drastically delayed: after prison uniform

indicators.note: 'after' puts the words before it behind the words that follow it, so the prison and uniform come first

blocks.note: jug is slang for jail
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a delayed train is late

explanation.surface: A police arrest held up badly because someone had to change into prison uniform first.
explanation.walkthrough: JUG + U + LATE. Jugulate literally means to cut the throat, and figuratively to stop something by violent measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers glosses jugulate as checking or suppressing something by drastic means, which is stopping it violently.

clue.text: With jars holding one gallon, judges turn up

indicators.note: something holding another item has it inside, so one piece sits within the pair
in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge, doubled for the plural
Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for gallon
your turn in a game is your go

explanation.surface: Jars holding a gallon arrive for the judges to taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jars' looks like a noun for containers, but the definition is an adverb phrase meaning with jolts. 'Turn up' splits: turn is the go, and up reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jig-jog describes a jolting, jogging motion, so it means with jars and bumps.

clue.text: March girl up with woolly coat off and stop

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the name is read from the bottom
having the coat off means the fleece is removed, a sheep stripped

blocks.note: Meg is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a woolly animal with its coat off has been shorn

explanation.surface: A girl on a march with her woolly coat off has to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: MEG reversed + SHORN. 'March' looks like walking, but it is the family surname in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemshorn is an organ stop with a tone like the old horn-shaped flute of the same name.

clue.text: See tailless parasite in running water

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A tailless parasite is spotted swimming in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: LO + TIC(K). The definition takes in 'in', describing what lives in a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotic is the ecological term for things living in or relating to flowing water such as rivers.

clue.text: Blue, inverted, crowned at the edges, like some corollas

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, so the letters run the other way
sitting at the edges means wrapping round, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling low
crowned in the sense of having its top covered

explanation.surface: A botanist describes flowers that are blue, upside down and tipped with colour at their edges.
explanation.walkthrough: T(WOL)IPPED. 'Crowned' and 'blue' sound like botanical description, which suits the flower definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-lipped corolla, as in snapdragons and sage, has its petals fused into upper and lower lips.

clue.text: Twig — stick with fancy point — makes sense in Highlands

indicators.note: 'fancy' as an adjective means elaborate or made-up, so the following word is rearranged

blocks.note: to twig and to rumble both mean to see through or understand
gum is something that sticks
the five letters of point, rearranged

explanation.surface: A walking-stick with a decorative point is an oddly sensible thing to have in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' and 'stick' read as bits of wood, but both are verbs here. Rumblegumption is a Scots form of rumgumption, common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumblegumption is a Scottish word for shrewdness or common sense, hence sense as spoken in the Highlands.

clue.text: Fine to grasp sensitive part in extract from book or cheap film

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it inside, so one word wraps another
'in' places that combined piece inside the extract

blocks.note: a quote is a passage taken from a book
A1 means first-rate or fine, written here as AI
the quick is the tender flesh under a fingernail

explanation.surface: A fine reader grasps the sensitive part of a passage from a book, or from a cheap film.
explanation.walkthrough: QUOT(A(QUICK)I)E. A1, taken as AI, is the old shipping-register mark for top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Quota quickies were cheap, rapidly made British films produced to meet a 1927 law on home-made screen quotas.

clue.text: Double salt initially mixed into bitter soup

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for only the opening letter of the word it follows
'into' says one piece goes inside the others, here between the beer and the soup

blocks.note: bitter is a kind of British beer, an ale
first letter of mixed
broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: Salt has been stirred twice into a bitter soup by a heavy-handed cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' sounds like an instruction to use the salt twice, but it belongs to the definition. Bitter is a British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alembroth, the alchemists' 'salt of wisdom', is a double chloride of mercury and ammonium, a compound of two salts.

clue.text: In pursuit of tips on cloth, one tries game wool supplier

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters
a pursuer comes behind, so the following pieces are placed after the cloth's ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of cloth
Roman numeral one
Rugby Union, the game in which tries are scored

explanation.surface: Someone after a supply of good fabric tries a game of seeking out a wool merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: CH + I + RU. 'Tries game' is a cryptic description of rugby, where a try is the main way of scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The chiru is the Tibetan antelope, whose fine underfur is the source of shahtoosh, a prized wool.

clue.text: Old mnemonic devices in Latin which matter

blocks.note: qui is the Latin for which or who
matter in the medical sense: pus from a wound

explanation.surface: A scholarly note on old memory aids explaining which matter they recorded, phrased in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: QUI + PUS. 'Matter' looks abstract but here means the discharge from an infected wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Quipus were Inca records of knotted cords, used to keep accounts and as memory aids for recording information.

clue.text: Seduce with hot text to Mrs Sprat?

blocks.note: in means fashionable, the hot thing
a phone message to Mrs Sprat: 'fat u ate', since she could eat no lean

explanation.surface: A cad tries to seduce Jack Sprat's wife by sending her a steamy text.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + FAT U ATE. In the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean; text-speak writes 'you' as U.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate is to inspire someone with a foolish passion, close to winning them over by seduction.

clue.text: Try and shoot bats

blocks.note: to have a crack at something is to try it
to pot is to shoot, as at game birds

explanation.surface: An instruction to try to shoot at some bats flying around at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: CRACK + POT. 'Bats' looks like a plural noun for the animals, but it is the informal adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for crazy, and crackpot as an adjective means eccentric or mad.

clue.text: Immigrant settlers in church plan to keep move on ice

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an aim is a plan or intention
a lutz is a jump in figure skating

explanation.surface: Newcomers to a parish meet in church to plan a skating outing.
explanation.walkthrough: CH + A(LUTZ)IM. The answer is a Hebrew plural, which is why it ends -IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalutzim were Jewish pioneers who emigrated to Palestine to work the land in agricultural settlements.

clue.text: Very good for ducks to be in?

definitions.text: Very good for ducks to be in?

indicators.note: something that is in another word sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: pious means very good in the religious sense
duck and luv are both northern English terms of endearment, like dear

explanation.surface: Someone asks what kind of weather would suit ducks perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, recalling the British saying 'lovely weather for ducks' on a rainy day. Ducks and luv are both affectionate forms of address in parts of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluvious is an old adjective meaning rainy, and wet weather is the kind ducks are said to enjoy.

clue.text: Sceptics misled — if nicely — about stocks

indicators.note: something that stocks goods keeps them inside, so the answer sits within the run of words
'about' as in turned about, so the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: a run of consecutive letters across these words, spanning the end of misled, all of if and the start of nicely

explanation.surface: People who doubt were led astray, however politely, about the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocks' looks like shares, tying to 'misled', but it is a verb meaning holds; read 'misled if nicely' backwards to see the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Infidels are unbelievers, people who reject a religious faith, so sceptics in the religious sense.

clue.text: Squaddy's haunt, regularly visited, recalled trading facility

indicators.note: calling at a place regularly means stopping at every other spot, so alternate letters are taken
something recalled is called back, so the kept letters run from the end

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of squaddys haunt

explanation.surface: A soldiers' old pub, regularly visited, has been remembered fondly.
explanation.walkthrough: A squaddy is a British private soldier. The even letters QADSAN, read backwards, give NASDAQ.
explanation.definitionFit: NASDAQ is the American electronic stock exchange, a facility for trading shares.

clue.text: Birth control pioneer promoting pill in East London terraces?

indicators.note: a promotion moves something up a rank, so one letter is shifted to an earlier place

blocks.note: Marie Stopes, who opened Britain's first birth-control clinic
E is slang for an ecstasy pill

explanation.surface: Marie Stopes campaigns for the contraceptive pill among the terraced streets of London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: In STOPES the E moves up one place before the P. East London here is the South African port city, not the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoep is the South African word for a raised veranda or terrace in front of a house.

clue.text: What's central to bellyache is keeping dry part of tongue

indicators.note: the central part of a word is its middle, here the middle three letters
keeping something is holding it inside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the middle three of the nine letters of bellyache
TT, teetotal, is a dry drinker

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a dry tongue is at the heart of their tummy trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: LY(TT)A. 'Dry' means abstaining from alcohol, and TT (teetotal) is the crossword abbreviation for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lytta is the worm-shaped strip of cartilage in the underside of the tongue of dogs and other carnivores.

clue.text: Motorists coming across tackle powerful dog

indicators.note: coming across something means spanning it from side to side, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: the Automobile Association, Britain's motoring organisation
tackle as in gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Drivers come across a powerful dog trying to tackle them.
explanation.walkthrough: A(KIT)A. 'Tackle' looks like a verb from football but is a noun meaning equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large, strong Japanese breed of spitz-type dog.

clue.text: Check out European city with one's cab drivers there?

blocks.note: to vet is to check
the Italian city
I for one; the 's is read as 'has' and joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A tip to look over an unfamiliar city and the taxi drivers who work there.
explanation.walkthrough: VET + TURIN + I. 'There' points back to the Italian city, so the drivers are Italian, and the answer is an Italian plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetturini are Italian drivers of hired carriages, the old-fashioned cabmen of Italy.

clue.text: Goddess's answer is one in patriarch's heart

indicators.note: 'is' here means becomes, so one letter stands in for another
the heart is the middle, so the swap happens among the central letters of the name

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
Roman numeral one
Isaac, the Old Testament patriarch, son of Abraham

explanation.surface: A goddess's answer is the key thing in a patriarch's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two As in the middle of ISAAC becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isiac is the adjective for Isis, the Egyptian goddess, so it means belonging to her.

clue.text: Producer Slavonicized, strangely, within Denmark's borders

indicators.note: doing something strangely means doing it oddly, so the long word is rearranged
'within' puts the rearranged letters inside the two edges of the country
a country's borders are its outer edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of Denmark
the twelve letters of slavonicized, rearranged

explanation.surface: A film producer's work has been oddly made Slavonic inside Denmark's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: D(AVID O SELZNIC)K. The anagram is the producer's name minus its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: David O Selznick was the Hollywood film producer behind Gone with the Wind and Rebecca.

clue.text: Vi, after drinking gin, back drying out

indicators.note: something that has been drinking has taken a liquid in, so one piece goes inside the other
'back' means going in the opposite direction, so the result is read from the end

blocks.note: VI is the Roman numeral six
a gin is a trap, a snare

explanation.surface: Vi, a woman back after a gin-drinking session, is drying out.
explanation.walkthrough: Vi reads as a woman's name but is a Roman numeral, and 'gin' is not the spirit but a trap for game.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeransis is a technical word for the process of drying up or becoming dry.

clue.text: Spot Russian spy dropping off article

indicators.note: to drop something off is to leave it behind, so letters are removed

blocks.note: Donald Maclean, the Cambridge spy who passed secrets to the Soviet Union
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Agents spot a Russian spy dropping off a piece of writing at a dead drop.
explanation.walkthrough: MACLEAN loses AN. Maclean was a British diplomat who spied for Moscow and defected in 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: A macle is a dark spot in a mineral such as chiastolite, so it serves for a spot or flaw.
